# CursorThemeManager

> **File:** `services/ui/CursorThemeManager.qml` · **Docs:** see [docs/dev](../../README.md)

The cursor theme as XCursor readers get it (the compositor's xcursor-theme, XCURSOR_THEME, GTK's cursor-theme). A theme naming its cursors only the X11 way (left_ptr, not default) and inheriting nothing shows the "default" theme's cursors (often Adwaita's) for the standard names it lacks, the arrow among them. So while the Input section's cursor part is on, scripts/cursor_theme.py makes a companion theme (axiom-cursor-<theme> in $XDG_DATA_HOME/icons/) inheriting it, with those names linked to its own cursors, and sets GTK's cursor-theme and cursor-size to what XCursor readers get. CompositorConfigManager hands that name on (CompositorLayer.input's `xcursor`); Hyprland's setcursor and the greeter keep the theme's own (docs/dev/compositor/config-modes.md).

### Properties

- `xcursorTheme` (readonly string): The name XCursor readers get for the theme set now: the companion theme where it fills names in, else the theme's own; "" while the cursor part is off or until it's known
- `ready` (readonly bool): Whether xcursorTheme has been known once (CompositorConfigManager waits for it at start, so it writes the name once)
- `companionPrefix` (readonly string): What a companion theme's name starts with (left out of the themes to pick)
